name: event-page
title: Event page
description: A page for one gathering: a reunion, a wedding, a party or a fundraiser. The next event's date, place and RSVP come first, each event a ticket with its schedule; changes and cancellations show in a banner and on the ticket, and past events fold away under Earlier.

images.purpose: a wide photo under the tickets that says what the event is: the group, the venue, an old class photo; without it the page goes straight from the tickets to the updates
images.alt_hint: what the photo shows, e.g. The class of 2007 on the school steps at graduation
images.prompt: a real photograph of {subject}; wide, sharp, people's faces visible; never generated

images.purpose: the event's emblem: a crest, monogram or save-the-date mark, shown large above the event name and small in the header and browser tab; flat, one colour, so it follows the palette
images.alt_hint: what the emblem shows, e.g. The Kestrel Falls crest with 07 under it
images.prompt: {subject} as a simple flat emblem or monogram, initials or a year only, in the palette's accent colour on a transparent ground

images.purpose: the picture when a link to the page is shared in messages; empty uses the hero
images.prompt: made from the hero photo, cropped to 1200x630

images.purpose: a photo at the top of an update or an event's own page, e.g. after-event photos
images.prompt: a real photograph from the event

content.purpose: the event's name, the big headline, e.g. Kestrel Falls High, Class of 2007: twenty years on

one stream (layout list) whose entries are events: each entry's event block {start, end, place, rsvp, schedule, status} makes a ticket at the top of the page, soonest first; past ones fold under Earlier. A second stream (layout feature) is the organisers' updates: the newest in full
one line of what, when and where, under the tickets
the main button under the tickets (with cta_link), usually RSVP; cta2_label and cta2_link make a second, e.g. Where to stay
the banner across the top for a change that can't wait, e.g. Changed: the picnic has moved to the pavilion; set until so it goes by itself
a short list of useful links under the tickets: hotel block, registry, photo upload, each with a note

cards in groups make the details: a group such as Good to know (questions as names, answers as descriptions, a price where it costs) and Where to stay (hotels with price and link); each group prints as its own section
the organisers' email and phone as big buttons at the end of the page
the footer line, e.g. the organising committee's name

art.ask: Ask your person for one wide photo that says what the event is: the group, the venue, an old class photo. Real photos only. If they want a crest or monogram, make it with them and keep it simple.
art.style: Photographs for the hero and covers. The optional emblem is a single flat shape or monogram in the palette's accent colour on a transparent ground; no words except initials or a year. Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
art.prompt_prefix: simple flat emblem, one colour, bold shapes, readable at 32 px, centred, no gradients, no photo-realism, no background.
steps: Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
Ask for the hero photo (photo_upload_link works from a phone). Check it is wide (at least 2080 px across), sharp, and that the people in it are happy to be shown.
Write its alt text with your person: what and who it shows, in a sentence.
Upload it to site.hero with site.hero_alt.

Optional emblem: agree the idea and use the palette's accent colour; make it from the emblem prompt (start with prompt_prefix); shrink it to 32 px and check it still reads; upload it to site.logo with site.logo_alt.
Call theme_needs: every slot you meant to fill should say filled.
